The main takeaway from our work is that

the S-matrix of the principal chiral model is not only consistent with the spectrum of the model, but it also correctly reproduces the energy of the ground state in the presence of an arbitrary background.

the S-matrix of a supersymmetric model may be constructed from the S-matrices of its bosonic and fermionic sectors, which in turn can be obtained from the S-matrices of their respective non-supersymmetric models.

a supersymmetric extension of the S-matrices for the non-supersymmetric principal chiral models is possible, provided the S-matricies are formulated on a space of states which is enlarged to include the RSOS kinks.
